overloads.semanticRole: Parses an XML document from a path/URL, optionally validating it against a DTD (either referenced inside the document or explicitly designated by the dtd parameter), and returns a document reference.

discriminatedBy.rule: Third parameter is a DTD pathname/text (or omitted to use any DTD/XSD reference found inside the document itself).

overloads.semanticRole: Parses an XML document from a path/URL, optionally validating it against an XML Schema (XSD) explicitly designated by the schema parameter.

discriminatedBy.rule: Third parameter is an XSD file/URL pathname, selected instead of the dtd overload to validate by schema rather than DTD.

constraints: Execution of DOM Parse XML source is synchronous.
document can be a full pathname, a Unix-style macOS path, an http(s)/ftp URL, or an empty string to prompt an Open File dialog.

If validation is True and the third parameter is omitted, validation is attempted via a DTD or XSD reference found inside the document itself; this can chain (a referenced DTD that itself references an XSD).
If validation cannot be performed (no DTD/XSD found, bad URL, etc.), an error is generated and reported via the Error system variable.
The returned reference must eventually be released by calling DOM CLOSE XML with it.

The dtd/schema overloads are not statically distinguishable by parameter type (both Text) -- 4D discriminates at runtime by file-extension convention (a ".dtd" path selects DTD validation, an ".xsd" path selects schema validation) or by content-sniffing (if the third parameter's text begins with "<?xml", it is treated as an inline DTD rather than a pathname).
Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): DOM XML document lifecycle: create/parse ref -> navigate/get/set elements and attributes -> export/close
